content.text: I can't see the exact defective line, because the retrieved snippet of `MailService.confirmNewEmail` elides its URL construction. The most likely cause is that it builds the link to `/confirm-email`, the sign-up activation page, instead of a dedicated new-email page such as `/confirm-new-email`.

candidates.explanation: The link in the new-email verification mail is built from the frontend domain plus '/confirm-email', the same path used by userSignUp. That is probably the bug, but the retrieved snippet elides this line, so I could not confirm it. The frontend page for '/confirm-email' calls POST auth/email/confirm (AuthService.confirmEmail). That method requires the user to be inactive and ignores the newEmail claim in the JWT. The link should go to a separate path such as '/confirm-new-email', which calls POST auth/email/confirm/new (AuthService.confirmNewEmail) and applies the email change. The i18n keys already use 'confirm-new-email.*', so the template and URL are probably copy-pasted from sign-up.

This is the secondary suspect. update signs the hash with the confirmEmailSecret and a newEmail claim, then hands it to mailService.confirmNewEmail. The part after the signing is elided, so I could not check how the mail is sent. If it calls userSignUp instead, or sends the wrong data, the user would get the sign-up style link.

fix.description: In MailService.confirmNewEmail, change the URL path from '/confirm-email' to '/confirm-new-email'. The frontend page for that path must call POST /auth/email/confirm/new with the hash. Also check that the template used is the new-email one, not activation.hbs.
